news.title: 'Sorry you were so consumed by hate' - Gianni Infantino blasts FIFA critics after 'most outstanding' World Cup
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has hit back at his detractors in extraordinary fashion, claiming that those who criticised the 2026 World Cup were "consumed by hate." In a lengthy and defiant statement, the head of world football’s governing body defended the tournament’s legacy and urged his opponents to "meditate or pray" instead of spreading negativity. In the wake of a tournament that was as much defined by its off-field drama as its on-field heroics, Infantino has chosen to go on the offensive. The FIFA president used his personal Instagram and the organisation’s official channels to deliver a stinging rebuke to the journalists and critics who questioned the logistics and integrity of the 2026 World Cup across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

news.title: Lopes Cabral's curling goal against Argentina voted FIFA World Cup's best goal
news.lede: Cape Verde added another chapter to its World Cup journey on Monday after Sidny Lopes Cabral won the public vote for the Goal of the Tournament.Lopes Cabral earned the honour for his curling strike into the top corner against Argentina during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The goal came in extra time of Cape Verde's Round of 32 match in Miami Gardens, drawing his side level at 2-2 against the defending champions. Argentina, however, went on to win the match 3-2. The 2026 edition marked Cape Verde's first appearance at the FIFA World Cup.

news.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino accuses critics of spreading hate at World Cup
news.lede: Infantino claims critics of World Cup ‘missed it all’. He again defends Balogun affair and treatment of Iran. The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has launched an extraordinary attack at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives, while defending the tournament as a success that celebrated unity, safety and inclusion. In a 15-part message published on Monday on Instagram, Infantino claimed detractors had overlooked the joy and togetherness experienced by millions of people around the world who witnessed the tournament, won by Spain and staged in the US, Canada and Mexico.

news.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Hot dog consumption worth 135 km, 6.8 million fans, 300,000 organising staff - the numbers behind the spectacle
news.lede: Getty Images Getty Images https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/eae7zb/article71274302.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/FIFA%20WORLD%20CUP%20Getty%20Images.jpg CHENNAI The FIFA World Cup 2026, held across three countries and 16 host cities over 39 days, showcased not only thrilling matches but also an unprecedented logistical feat that supported over 6.8 million fans. The FIFA World Cup 2026 saw some unforgettable football played, record attendances and historic moments on the pitch. The global administrative body, on Monday, released striking figures behind the organisation of the largest event of the sporting calendar this year, which was held in three countries across 39 days, involving 16 host cities, 48 team base camps and 645 official sites.

news.title: The 2026 World Cup is over, but the onslaught of soccer relentlessly rolls on | Leander Schaerlaeckens
news.lede: The supply of soccer seems to be enormously exceeding demand. It’s made the sport feel utterly overwhelming. On Friday, the Scottish Premiership kicks off its 2026-27 season. The following Friday, the Dutch Eredivisie begins anew, and England’s Carabao Cup sets off on its ponderous journey.

news.title: FIFA president's leaked letter to Argentina following World Cup Final brawl comes across as tone deaf
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup was a smashing success, but that doesn't mean certain aspects of the event should be off limits to criticism, and that's especially true when it comes to a recently leaked letter from FIFA president Gianni Infantino. Following Spain's extra-time win over Argentina in the World Cup Final, several different on-field brawls broke out between players and team staff members. Argentina's Leandro Paredes caught the most attention after appearing to grab Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat, which set off more back-and-forths around the pitch. Infantino either forgot that several Argentina members were involved in the on-field brawl, or is simply choosing to ignore that fact.

news.title: FIFA Gianni Infantino defends 2026 World Cup, slams critics for ‘spreading hate’
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino hit back hard at people criticizing the 2026 World Cup, accusing the “critics” of spreading hate and overlooking what he described as “the most outstanding FIFA World Cup.” Infantino’s comments came in a lengthy open letter published on his personal Instagram account and on FIFA’s official channels after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the final to lift the trophy. Infantino said many critics had focused on controversies instead of celebrating the tournament’s achievements. He said that millions of fans from all over the world came together during the month-long event jointly hosted by the U.S., Canada and Mexico.
